q: What does the 3 in y = 3x + 2 mean?
o: The line crosses the y-axis at 3
For each step of 1 to the right, y goes up by 3
why: 3 is the slope (rise per step to the right). The 2 is where the line crosses the y-axis.

q: A line with a bigger slope is higher on the graph.
why: Slope is steepness, not height. y = 3x is below y = x + 10 until x = 5.
1 − 7 = −6, so the slope is −6/3 = −2. The line goes down.

q: A horizontal line's slope is undefined.
why: Myth. A horizontal line has slope 0 (no rise). A vertical line has an undefined slope, because its run is 0 and you can't divide by 0.

q: Demand is Q = 100 − 2P. What does the −2 mean?
o: The price falls by 2 for each unit
Each rise of 1 in the price cuts the quantity by 2
why: It's the slope of Q against P: when P goes up by 1, Q changes by −2.
